name: thing
description: Anything that can be a 3D model. The conventions here apply to every model.
conventions: Units are metres. +Y is up. The front of the model faces +Z (Godot's Vector3.MODEL_FRONT, also the glTF convention), so the model's left side is +X.
The origin sits on the ground (y = 0), under the centre of the model or under the point a user will place it by.
Every part that moves gets its own node, with the node origin at its pivot. Use PascalCase names and keep sibling names unique.
Apply scale and rotation before export: scale 1 on every node, no negative scale.
Left and right halves are exact mirror images unless the object is asymmetric by design.
anticipate: A simple collision shape (a box or convex hull), not the visual mesh.
A triangle budget, and LODs for anything that will appear many times.
Few materials: every material is a draw call, so share textures where you can.
pitfalls: A model that is 100 times too big or small (a unit mistake) is the most common error: check the size against the typical range.
A moving part baked into the body mesh cannot be animated later.
